neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were strangers. A meeting was convened by a community group, and the victim and others were passing by the accused's house when they were attacked. The accused inflicted a knife blow on the victim's chest, causing him to fall and die instantly. Other accused inflicted sword blows and blows with a cycle chain. The victim's body was sent for post-mortem examination, which confirmed the cause of death as syncope due to shock and hemorrhage from the stab wound. The injured were sent to the hospital for medical examination and treatment. The prosecution presented evidence including medical reports and eyewitness accounts, while the accused claimed self-defense and that the victim was the aggressor.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that accused Gopal deserves to be convicted under Section 302 IPC, even though he might have inflicted only a single injury on the chest of Mitthulal, as Mitthulal died instantaneously, showing the nature and force of the injury. The prosecution also contended that other accused persons could not have been convicted only under Section 324 IPC, as the injuries sustained by the complainant party were serious in nature, and the sentence of period already undergone with fine was too lenient.

quotes.text: It was further contended that Mitthulal had died instantaneously which shows the nature and the force with which the injury was caused by accused Gopal on the chest of Mitthulal
It was further contended that other accused persons could not have been convicted only under Section 324 IPC, whereas the injuries sustained by the complainant party were serious in nature

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the complainant party was the aggressor and that the accused acted in self-defence. It was also contended that the prosecution failed to explain the injuries sustained by Shankarlal and Gopal, and that the complainant party attacked the accused Shankarlal and Gopal while returning to Ratlam, causing injuries to them.

quotes.text: It was contended by learned counsel for the accused Gopal that the prosecution has failed to explain the injuries sustained by Shankarlal and Gopal and the complainant party was aggressor
They, therefore, had acted in self defence

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the ends of justice should be met, and that the conviction of accused Gopal under Section 304 Part-I IPC should be upheld, but his sentence should be reduced to the period already undergone by him, which was more than six years.

quotes.text: Held: Conviction of appellant-accused uls. 304 (Part I) upheld, however, in order to meet the ends of justice, his sentence reduced to period already undergone which was more than 6 years

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed to meet the ends of justice, reducing the sentence of accused Gopal to the period already undergone by him, which was more than six years.
